I wonder how does Doom 4 compare to this.

Doom 4 was never released. What we've got now is DOOM and it is a very different game. Much more focussed on open space battles rather than cramped corridor and scary things jumping out at you. I remember playing Doom 3 when it first came out and even thought my hardware was barely able to run it, I still had to play it in short bursts because of the constant adrenalin. With DOOM I'm not having that same experience. As long as you keep moving around the current slaughter ground and keep firing you'll eventually clear it and be able to poke around and find the various items. That's not to say I'm not enjoying the new version, I certainly am, but it feels more like the original Doom and Doom 2 whereas Doom 3 was a bit of a departure as it was this very cramped and claustrophobic feel.
I think the cancelled version should have been DooM and the released version should have been called Doom 4.

If anything (as I'm still working through it) the new one is so much more like the original than Doom 3 was that it is really a reboot so I wouldn't think Doom 4 would make sense. I'm really enjoying the game though and as I said, it doesn't scare me like Doom 3 did. There are occasions where I walk into an area and I think "yeah, here's a big open area with lots of ammo and powerups, I wonder what comes next (NOT!)" and then the baddies descend and sometimes I struggle to get the weapons in the right order to succeed and other times I outright slaughter them. Just keep moving. It is very like the original. I wouldn't object to a torch like Doom 3 had though.....

The new Doom is vastly superior to Doom 3 for a lot of these same reasons, but it's on the 'superior' side of the old school shooter rather than the 'lesser' end of it.

The first couple levels kind of feel a little like Serious Sam, but it quickly moves away from that once you get past the 'we're teaching you how the mechanics and environments work' segments that are the first level and a half or so of the game. After that, it's pure balls to the wall 90's era shooter goodness, but with modern graphics and interfaces.

Multiplayer is bland, but not awful, and the Snap-Map stuff kind of makes up for that. Plus, the secrets unlock classic Doom levels you can run around in that use the old school maps and graphics for the environments, but utilize the newer enemies and weapons.

Plus a nice sense of progression with upgrades you get along the way. Some of which are quite fun and useful.﻿ There are several different kinds, player upgrades, armor upgrades, weapon upgrades, and runes that each add different effects, and they can also be ignored if you really want to go completely purist.

Fun stuff, has that old school vibe but still manages to feel like a modern game.
